ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Unlock an element the canvas refuses to select
ux.finding: Lock is stored in two places that never reconcile. The padlock a user sees is drawn from a per-page localStorage list; the lock the canvas enforces is a flag on the element in the project. Clicking the padlock writes both, but the panel only ever RE-READS localStorage. Open the same project in a different browser, on a different machine, or after clearing site data, and a locked element is still locked in the document — the canvas refuses to select it and tells the user to 'Unlock it in the Layers panel' — while the Layers panel draws an open padlock. The instruction points at a control that shows the opposite state.
ux.evidence: useLayerActions.ts:70-97 hydrateFromStorage reads loadSetFromStorage(pageId,'locked') and pushes it INTO the engine (`storedLocked.forEach(id => composer.elements.getElement(id)?.setLocked(true))`) — it never reads element.isLocked() back. layersPersistence.ts:8-9 documents the keys `buildrick-layers-{pageId}-locked` / `-hidden`. useLayerActions.ts:167 `composer?.elements.getElement(pending.id)?.setLocked(pending.locked)`. Element.ts:152-153 setLocked writes this.data.locked; shared/types/element.ts:73-74 declares `locked?: boolean` on ElementData, so it travels with the document. useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95 is the canvas refusal + that exact toast copy. Searched: 'lockedIds', 'setLocked', 'isLocked', 'loadSetFromStorage', 'buildrick-layers'.
ux.fix: The element is the source of truth for lock. Layers should read it, not a browser-local mirror — otherwise the one control the product names as the way out of a locked element can display the wrong state.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.finding: Lock means two different things depending on which surface you click. Clicking a locked element on the canvas is refused with a toast. Clicking the same element's row in the Layers tree selects it normally, and the Inspector then edits it like anything else — so the lock a user set to protect an element protects it from exactly one of the two ways of reaching it.
ux.evidence: useLayerSelection.ts:68-74 selectSingle -> `composer.selection.select(el)` with no lock check; selectLayer (:76-110) has none either. useSelectionBehavior.ts:88-95 and :106-118 both return early on `element.isLocked()` with the toast. LayerTreeItem.tsx:196-197 blocks only double-click rename on locked rows (`onDoubleClick={(e) => { if (!isLocked) onStartEditing(...) }}`); the row's onClick (:187-189) is unguarded. Searched: 'isLocked', 'lockedIds.has', 'selection.select', 'canDrag'.
ux.fix: Decide what lock protects and apply it on both surfaces. Selecting a locked layer to inspect it is defensible — editing it silently is not; if Layers can select it, the Inspector must show it as locked with an unlock affordance.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: See at a glance which elements are hidden on mobile or tablet
ux.finding: The Layers tree draws 'M' and 'T' badges for elements hidden at the mobile and tablet breakpoints, and they can never appear. The tree nodes are built from a five-field shape that does not include the override data the badge reads, so the field is always undefined. The result is that the Inspector's per-breakpoint Visibility switch — the one that actually removes an element from the published page at a given width — has no echo anywhere in the structural view.
ux.evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:276-281 renders the badges from `layer.breakpointOverrides?.mobile?.hidden` / `?.tablet?.hidden`. useLayerTree.ts:88-95 buildTree returns exactly { id, type, tagName, depth, preview, children } — no breakpointOverrides. Searched: 'breakpointOverrides', 'bdc-lr-bp', 'Hidden on mobile', 'buildTree'. Confirms and extends a finding from another lane.
ux.fix: Feed the breakpoint state into the tree node, or drop the badge. A responsive-visibility decision that is invisible in Layers is a decision the user cannot audit before publishing.

ux.screen: Layers panel · tree row eye toggle
ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.finding: The panel has an eye icon that does not hide anything on the site. It sets an editor-only dimming attribute on the canvas node; the element publishes exactly as before. Hiding an element from the published page is a different control in a different panel (the Inspector's Visibility section). The tooltips now say so — 'Dim in editor — the element still publishes' — but the icon is the universal symbol for hide, so the copy is fighting the glyph, and the two controls have no visible relationship to each other.
ux.evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:285-297 the block comment and the tooltip strings 'Dim in editor — the element still publishes' / 'Show in editor — this element publishes either way'. useLayerActions.ts:126-146 toggleVisibility sets state and, in an effect, `el.setAttribute('data-hidden', ...)` on the DOM node only — nothing touches the element model or the export. Searched: 'toggleVisibility', 'data-hidden', 'hiddenIds', 'isPageLive'.
ux.fix: One idea, one control. Either the eye drives real per-breakpoint visibility (and the Inspector reflects it), or it stops using an eye — a preview/dim affordance should not wear the icon that every other tool uses for publish-visibility.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Name my layers so the tree is readable, then hand the file to a teammate
ux.finding: Custom layer names are browser-local. They are written to localStorage under the page id and are never part of the project, so the names a designer spends an afternoon setting are invisible to a teammate, gone on a different machine, and gone when site data is cleared. Nothing in the rename flow says this, and the write fails silently when storage is full or disabled.
ux.evidence: useLayerActions.ts:120-124 persists customNames via saveMapToStorage(currentPageId, customNames); layersPersistence.ts:73-79 saveMapToStorage writes `buildrick-layers-{pageId}-names` inside a try/catch whose comment reads 'localStorage might be full or disabled - silently fail'. useLayerActions.ts:180-199 saveEditedName only updates the local Map and emits ELEMENT_RENAMED for the status bar. Searched: 'customNames', 'saveMapToStorage', 'ELEMENT_RENAMED', 'getDisplayName'.
ux.fix: A layer name is document content, not a browser preference. Persist it with the element; until then the rename affordance should say the name is local to this browser.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Delete a section from the page
ux.finding: Right-click → Delete on a layer removes the element and every descendant instantly — no confirmation, no count of what is going, and no toast afterwards. Deleting the top section of a page takes one click from a menu whose Delete row sits directly under Duplicate. The panel's multi-select banner has an inline confirm for the same act, so the safer path is the one used less often.
ux.evidence: useLayerActions.ts:208-217 deleteLayer: beginTransaction, removeElement, endTransaction, onConfirm() — no dialog, no child count. The file's own header comment at useLayerActions.ts:8 claims 'Delete with child count confirmation'. LayerContextMenu.tsx:86-88 is the menu row. index.tsx:79 `const [pendingBannerDelete, setPendingBannerDelete]` is the banner's inline confirm, used only by LayerSelectionBanner. Searched: 'deleteLayer', 'pendingBannerDelete', 'confirm', 'removeElement'.
ux.fix: Name the blast radius before deleting — 'Delete Section and 24 elements inside it?' — or at minimum confirm the deletion afterwards with an undo, the way Media's delete does.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Delete or duplicate several selected layers at once
ux.finding: With five layers selected, right-clicking one of them acts on that ONE row for Cut, Copy, Duplicate, Delete and Rename, but on the whole selection for Group. The menu gives no sign which scope any item uses, and the selection stays highlighted throughout, so the user watches five highlighted rows and one of them disappear.
ux.evidence: useLayerContextActions.ts:16-19 every case except 'group' and 'selectChildren' is keyed on the `nodeId` argument (serializeElement(nodeId), deleteLayer(nodeId,...), duplicateLayer(nodeId)); case 'group' at :97-99 uses `[...selectionHook.selectedIds]`. LayerContextMenu.tsx:20 receives selectedCount and uses it only to disable Group (:95). Searched: 'selectedIds', 'nodeId', 'LayerAction', 'groupLayers'.
ux.fix: A context menu opened on a row inside a multi-selection should act on the selection, and should say so ('Delete 5 layers'). One menu with two silently different scopes is how people lose work.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Walk the layer tree with the keyboard
ux.finding: Arrow keys in the tree change the canvas selection but never move keyboard focus, so the tree cannot be walked. Pressing Down once selects the row below the focused row; pressing Down again selects the same row again, because focus never left the row you started on. There is no way to step through the tree without a mouse.
ux.evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:155-164 — ArrowDown/ArrowUp compute nextId from `visibleIds.indexOf(layer.id)` (the row that owns the handler) and call `onSelect(nextId, {})`; there is no focus() call. grep for '.focus()' across panels/layers/index.tsx, LayerTreeItem.tsx and hooks/ returns exactly one hit, useLayerActions.ts:175, which focuses the rename input. index.tsx:180-186 scrollToSelection only scrolls. Searched: 'ArrowDown', 'focus()', 'getVisibleLayerIds', 'roving', 'tabIndex'.
ux.fix: Move focus with the arrow keys and let selection follow focus (or follow on Enter). This is the standard tree pattern and the panel already declares role=tree/treeitem.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Tab past the Layers panel to reach the canvas or the Inspector
ux.finding: Every layer row is its own tab stop, and each row also contains up to three more focusable buttons (chevron, eye, lock). On a page with 80 elements that is over 200 presses of Tab to get out of the panel. A keyboard user cannot leave Layers in any reasonable number of keystrokes.
ux.evidence: LayerTreeItem.tsx:172 `tabIndex={0}` on the treeitem div — unconditional, one per row. The chevron Button (:200-206) sets tabIndex={-1} only when the row has no children; the eye (:301-311) and lock (:324-333) Buttons set no tabIndex at all and are native buttons. index.tsx:428 declares role='tree' on the container. Searched: 'tabIndex', 'role="treeitem"', 'roving', 'aria-activedescendant'.
ux.fix: One tab stop for the whole tree (roving tabindex or aria-activedescendant), with the row actions reachable from the focused row rather than each being its own stop.

ux.screen: Layers panel · tree row eye/lock buttons
ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Hide or lock the layer I am pointing at
ux.finding: The old defect where 40px controls sat in 28px rows — so a click on the eye landed on the wrong layer — is FIXED: the buttons are now 20x20 inside a 28px row. What remains is that 20x20 is under the 24x24 minimum for a pointer target, and the row has the height to give it: two controls that toggle state on the wrong element are still a mis-click that a user may not notice.
ux.evidence: styles/layers-v2.css:157-168 — the comment reads 'Before: 40px controls in 28px rows, and elementFromPoint at…' and the rule now sets width/height 20px, min-height 0, padding 2px on .bdc-lr .bdc-lr-eye and .bdc-lr-lock. styles/layers-v2.css:17-27 .bdc-lr height 28px, padding 0 8px. LayerTreeItem.tsx:110-118 indent ladder base 12 step 16, matching the brief. Searched: 'bdc-lr-eye', 'bdc-lr-lock', 'elementFromPoint', 'height: 20px'.
ux.fix: Take the row's full 24px of usable height for both toggles. The regression is fixed; the target is still smaller than the guidance for a control whose mis-click silently changes a different element.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Move an element into a different container by dragging its layer row
ux.finding: A refused drop explains itself in raw type names and then vanishes. 'text cannot be nested inside heading' and 'button cannot contain children' are the element type ids, not the names the user sees on the rows, and the message clears itself after three seconds whether or not it was read. A locked container refuses a drop with a message but the row shows no locked-target affordance during the drag.
ux.evidence: index.tsx:120-135 showDropError('Cannot drop inside a locked container'), `${parentType} cannot contain children`, `${sourceType} cannot be nested inside ${parentType}` — parentType/sourceType come straight from getType(). index.tsx:87-93 auto-clears dropFeedback after 3000ms. LayerTreeItem.tsx:180-186 sets no drop-refused styling on the target row; data-drop only carries before/after/inside. Searched: 'showDropError', 'dropFeedback', 'canNestElement', 'data-drop'.
ux.fix: Say it in the words on the row ('A Heading can't hold other elements'), show the refusal on the target row during the drag rather than after the drop, and let the message stay until the user moves on.

ux.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
ux.task: Find every layer that is currently hidden or locked, or clear all locks
ux.finding: Hide and lock are per-row toggles with no roll-up anywhere. The footer counts total and selected layers only, so a user who locked six things across a long page has no way to find them again except by scrolling the whole tree, and no way to clear them in one move. Search matches names and types, not state.
ux.evidence: LayersTab.tsx:216-221 the footer renders only `${stats.selected} selected of ${stats.total}` or `${stats.total} layers`; stats come from index.tsx:63-67 which emits { total, selected } and nothing else. LayersTab.tsx:176-184 the header's three buttons are Expand all, Collapse all, Display settings. useLayerSearch.ts itemMatches is name/type based. Searched: 'stats-change', 'hiddenIds.size', 'lockedIds.size', 'Expand all', 'itemMatches'.
ux.fix: Count hidden and locked in the footer and make each count a filter, with an 'unlock all' escape. State a user can set on 200 rows needs a way to see and undo it that is not scrolling.

summary.purpose: Layers is the structural view of the current page — find, name, reorder, hide, lock and select the elements that make up the document.
summary.finding: PURPOSE: show the current page as a tree so a user can find, name, reorder and protect elements that are hard to hit on the canvas. PRIMARY TASKS: locate an element (search, expand/collapse all, auto-expand to the selection); select one or several; rename; reorder by drag; hide (editor-only dimming) and lock; cut/copy/paste/duplicate/delete/group from the right-click menu; copy a deep link to an element. ENTRY POINTS: the rail's Layers tab (LayersTab -> LayersPanel); a canvas selection auto-expands ancestors and scrolls the row into view (index.tsx:189-200); `layers:expand-all` / `layers:collapse-all` from the tab header. EXIT POINTS: selecting a row drives the canvas and the Inspector; the empty state's 'Open Insert' link hands off to Insert (LayersEmptyState.tsx:26-33); Copy link produces a URL that reopens the editor on this element. HANDS OFF TO: canvas + inspector (selection is the shared object, composer.selection is SSOT), engine history (every structural action wraps beginTransaction/endTransaction). RECEIVES FROM: canvas (selection, hover highlight), pages (a page change rebuilds the tree and re-reads that page's stored state), components (the instance badge). THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: three of the panel's own concepts — lock, hide and custom names — live in per-page localStorage rather than in the document, so the tree can disagree with the engine, with the canvas and with a teammate; and the panel is not keyboard-operable in the way its own role=tree markup promises.
summary.evidence: index.tsx:47-77, :189-200; LayersTab.tsx:113-126 (stats), :138-142 (expand/collapse events); layersPersistence.ts:8-9 (the three localStorage keys); useLayerTree.ts:99-105 (page-change rebuild); useLayerSelection.ts:43-66 (composer selection mirror). Searched: 'layers:stats-change', 'layers:expand-all', 'buildrick-layers', 'role="tree"', 'SELECTION_ADDED'.
summary.fix: Move lock, hide and layer names into the document so the tree, the canvas and a teammate cannot disagree, and give the tree the roving-focus keyboard behaviour its role=tree markup already promises.
